title: Wheel and tire specifications
introduction:
I use this page to answer three practical questions: which service materials are listed, where to find tire-inflation and wheel-weight guidance, and which torque reference applies to the fastener in hand. A small sensor screw and a wheel nut have very different jobs; sharing a wheel does not make their tightening requirements interchangeable.

Read the item name before choosing a torque-unit column. The columns express the same setting in different units, rather than successive tightening stages. The materials list identifies products but supplies no application locations or quantities. This page is a specification reference; use the matching service procedure for installation and material application.

edits.why: Match each product name to its listed specification code. A dash in Fill Capacity supplies no amount to apply, and inclusion in this table alone does not establish where a product belongs.

I obtain the tire-inflation specification from the Safety Certification Label on the driver door jamb. For wheel weights, use the wheel-weight manufacturer's rim gauge to determine the correct application. Think of that gauge as a shoe fitting for the rim: visual resemblance alone does not establish the right fit.

TPMS means tire pressure monitoring system. The numeric torque row applies specifically to the valve stem-to-TPMS sensor screw; select the column matching the torque tool's units. For wheel nuts, obtain the Wheel and Tire procedure identified in the table before tightening them. This sheet refers that operation onward and supplies neither its torque value nor its installation sequence.
